Theme

Latin word

aditus

aditus, aditūs m.

noun, fourth declension

access, approach; the right to approach; an approach, an entrance; gate

In this lexicon

  • access

    the recommended word · classical · Gell. 16.5.3: per quem ā viā aditus accessusque ad aedīs est; Ov. Rem. 120: difficilēs aditūs

  • entry

    also used · classical · Phaedr. 5.9.1: angustō in aditū; Caes. B.G. 4.20; Liv. 36.10 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 310

  • gate

    the recommended word · modern · Traupman 216; Traupman 320

Examples

  • locum ante jānuam domūs vacuum, per quem ā viā aditus accessusque ad aedīs est

    the open space in front of the door of a house, through which there is access from the street to the houseGell. 16.5.3

    In the entry for access

  • dum furor in cursū est, currentī cēde furōrī; difficilēs aditūs impetus omnis habet

    while the rage is running, give way to it as it runs: every outburst is hard to get nearOv. Rem. 119–120

    In the entry for access

  • Ad aditum duodecimum oecus erat praestōlātōrius, sellīs multīs īnstrūctus

    At gate twelve there was a waiting room with many seatscomposed

    In the entry for gate
